text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired for service `inference-prod-routing` -> incident INC123456. Pager delivered to schedule `contractors-night` (schedule_id: SCHED-OLD-987). Source: alertmanager webhook. Severity: P1. https://pagerduty.example/INC123456

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC123456 created by integration `alertmanager-prod`. First notification: contractors-night (SCHED-OLD-987).

Ben: Acked in PD. I'm oncall for prod-rotation but not the contractors-night schedule. :raising_hand: Seeing weird target.

Alice: Seeing a spike in 503/504 from runtime-gateway at 00:12 UTC. Grafana: https://grafana/example/d/abcd. Errors correlate with an increase in request timeouts to model-serving nodes.

Carol: Quick glance in PD — looks like a schedule ID mismatch. We renamed `prod-night` -> `prod-night-2026` during the last ops rename, but the alertmanager config still references the old schedule ID. PD shows both schedules present.

Devon: Support: 4 orgs reporting degraded inference (timeouts), ~20 requests/min failing per org. No data loss, but user-facing latency bump and retries. Customer names: acme, globex, exampleco, datacorp.

Ben: Status check — is this a routing problem (wrong responders) or a real service outage? If wrong responders, can we pause the PD integration temporarily to stop pages and handle alerts in-channel?

Maya: I can run a status page update once we know impact. Holding off until we confirm scope.

Alice: Mitigation suggestion (fast): 1) override escalation to prod-sre-manual 2) pause Alertmanager -> PagerDuty webhook 3) fix schedule ID reference in routing service and Alertmanager config, then re-enable.

Ben: I'll apply the override and pause the webhook now. Posting commands I plan to run:```bash
# pause the webhook in Alertmanager (temporary)
curl -X POST https://alertmanager.example/-/silences -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"service","value":"inference-prod-routing"}],"startsAt":"now","endsAt":"in 10m","createdBy":"oncall"}'

# update PD service escalation policy (example)
curl -X PUT "https://api.pagerduty.com/services/PSVXXXXX" \\
  -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"service":{"escalation_policy_id":"P-SRE-MANUAL"}}'
```

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC123456 acknowledged by Ben. Escalation policy changed to `P-SRE-MANUAL` by Ben.

Ben: Paused webhook and applied escalation override. Confirming pages should stop. :white_check_mark:

Carol: Deploying hotfix to mapping service to swap the old schedule ID to the canonical one and update a small shim used by alertmanager. PR merged: https://git.example/r/inference/ops/merge/3456. Deploying to canary -> prod.

Carol: Deploy log: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/pd-mapping` -> canary healthy -> rolling to prod.

Alice: After the override + pause + mapping fix, error rate is trending down. 503 rate back to baseline over the last 4m. Grafana link updated.

Devon: Sent initial customer note via status page that we saw elevated latency and a mitigation is in progress. No SLA breaches expected but followup will confirm.

Maya: Status page posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2026-03-14-inference-latency. Email to account leads sent.

Ben: Re-enabled Alertmanager webhook now that mapping is fixed. Watching for any re-fanout.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC123456 resolved (auto) after no new alerts within the quiet window. Marking resolved — please file follow-up actions.

Alice: Quick postmortem notes: root cause = stale schedule_id in alertmanager webhook after schedule rename during ops cleanup. Contributing factors: no automated inventory test for schedule IDs, ambiguous schedule names that led to manual rename without sweeping references. Impact: ~20m of elevated 503s, 4 affected customers, no data loss.

Ben: Action items (assigned):
- SRE: run schedule-id inventory across PD services (script + PR) -> https://git.example/r/inference/ops/pd-scripts#L12 (Ben)
- Devex/Eng: add CI check that validates PD schedule IDs referenced by alertmanager (Carol)
- Support: confirm customer followups and update status page with root cause (Maya/Devon)
- Oncall docs: add one-click PD override runbook and rehearsal (Alice)

Carol: I'll open the PR for the CI check this afternoon. Also cleaning up legacy schedule names to reduce ambiguity.

Maya: I'll send the follow-up message to customer account leads summarizing mitigation and next steps.

Ben: Closing thread for now. Reopen if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:

alice: adding note to retrospective doc and linking to this thread. :spiral_note_pad:
